title: Texture
about: Collocations for describing how things feel: dry or greasy hair, a bumpy flight, tender meat, a blunt knife, coarse salt. Also verbs such as melt, thaw and go soft, and texture words used about people and situations, like a sharp tongue or a sticky situation.

parts.title: Adjectives and their opposites for describing textures
Other texture words with their collocations

items.pattern: dry skin / hair · a cream / shampoo for dry skin / hair · opposite: oily skin, greasy hair
items.meaning: skin or hair without enough natural oil, so it feels rough or looks dull
items.example: Central heating always gives me **dry skin** in winter.
more: My **hair** gets **dry** and frizzy if I use a hairdryer every day.
This hand cream is for very **dry skin**, so it's quite thick.

items.pattern: greasy hair · also oily hair · hair gets / looks greasy · opposite: dry hair
items.meaning: hair with too much natural oil, so it looks dirty and flat soon after washing
items.example: Hot, humid weather always gives me **greasy hair**.
more: By the end of the camping trip, we all had **greasy hair** and muddy boots.
Gel can make your **hair** look **greasy** if you use too much.
items.watchOut: «Жирне волосся» — greasy або oily hair, не fat hair і не fatty hair: fat — товстий, fatty — жирний про їжу (fatty meat). Greasy звучить негативніше: волосся виглядає брудним.

items.pattern: oily skin · also greasy skin · opposite: dry skin
items.meaning: skin that produces a lot of natural oil, so it looks shiny
items.example: I've had **oily skin** since I was a teenager.
more: People with **oily skin** often get fewer wrinkles later in life.
In hot weather my **oily skin** gets even shinier, so I wash my face twice a day.
items.watchOut: «Жирна шкіра» — oily skin (іноді greasy skin), не fat skin і не fatty skin.

items.pattern: smooth skin / surface / complexion · feel / become smooth · opposite: rough
items.meaning: even and pleasant to touch, with no lumps, holes or rough areas
items.example: Use this scrub once a week for **smooth skin**.
more: The ice rink had a perfectly **smooth surface** first thing in the morning.
Her grandmother still had a **smooth complexion** at ninety.
items.watchOut: Complexion /kəmˈplekʃn/ — шкіра обличчя, її колір і стан, а не «комплекція» (статура — build): She has a smooth complexion.

items.pattern: rough skin / hands / surface / complexion · opposite: smooth
items.meaning: not smooth: hard, dry or uneven to touch
items.example: Gardening without gloves gives me **rough skin** on my hands.
more: The old wooden bench had a **rough surface** that caught on my jeans.
Sandpaper has one **rough** side and one smooth side.
items.watchOut: «Шорсткий, грубий на дотик» — rough. Rude — грубий у поведінці (a rude waiter); про шкіру чи поверхню так не кажуть.

items.pattern: a calm / smooth sea · calm / smooth water · the sea is calm · opposite: a choppy / rough sea
items.meaning: water with no waves or only very small ones
items.example: We kayaked across **smooth water** to the little island.
more: The captain promised us a **calm sea** for the trip back.
Early in the morning **the lake** is perfectly **smooth**.
items.watchOut: «Спокійне море» — зазвичай a calm sea, також smooth. Quiet sea кажуть рідко: quiet — передусім про звук.

items.pattern: a choppy / rough sea · choppy / rough water · rough seas · the sea gets rough
items.meaning: water with lots of small waves (choppy) or big, strong waves (rough), uncomfortable for boats
items.example: We had to turn the boat back because the **sea** was getting **rough**.
more: The lake gets **choppy** when the wind blows from the north.
Small fishing boats stay in the harbour when **the sea is rough**.
items.watchOut: Неспокійне, хвилясте море — choppy (дрібні часті хвилі) або rough (великі хвилі), не wavy: wavy hair — хвилясте волосся. Морська хвороба — seasickness.

items.pattern: a smooth road / flight / ride / journey · opposite: bumpy
items.meaning: even, with no shaking or jolting, so it's comfortable to travel on
items.uk: рівна дорога / спокійний політ, без трясіння
items.example: Cycling is a pleasure now that the **road** is **smooth** all the way to the village.
more: It was such a **smooth flight** that I slept most of the way.
Let's take the main road: it's longer but much **smoother**.
items.watchOut: «Рівна дорога» без вибоїн — a smooth road. Flat road — дорога без підйомів. «Спокійний політ» — зазвичай a smooth flight, а не a calm flight.

items.pattern: a bumpy road / flight / ride / journey · opposite: smooth
items.meaning: full of bumps or turbulence, so you get shaken about
items.example: My bike has no suspension, so I feel every hole on this **bumpy road**.
more: Fasten your seat belts: the next part of the **flight** may be **bumpy**.
The children love the **bumpy ride** in the back of Grandad's old jeep.
items.watchOut: Тряско — bumpy, не shaky: shaky — тремтячий, хиткий (shaky hands, a shaky chair). Турбулентність — turbulence, а такий політ — a bumpy flight.

items.pattern: a soft pillow / bed / mattress · soft ground · opposite: firm / hard
items.meaning: pleasant to lie or step on because it gives a little under your weight
items.uk: м'яка подушка / м'яке ліжко / м'яка земля
items.example: The hotel had huge **soft pillows**, and I slept like a baby.
more: After the rain, the **ground** was **soft** enough to dig.
I can't sleep on a **soft bed**; I wake up with backache.
items.watchOut: М'який на дотик — soft. Mild — м'який про погоду, смак чи характер (mild weather, a mild curry), про подушку так не кажуть.

items.pattern: a firm / hard pillow / bed / mattress · hard ground · opposite: soft
items.meaning: not soft: firm means pleasantly solid with good support, hard often means uncomfortable
items.example: My doctor says a **firm mattress** is better for a bad back.
more: Grandma likes a **firm pillow** that keeps her head high.
Wear proper boots: the **ground** is **hard** and stony up there.
items.watchOut: «Жорсткий матрац» — a firm або hard mattress, не tough і не strict: tough — про м'ясо, strict — суворий (про людей, правила). Firm звучить позитивно (добра підтримка), hard — частіше як скарга.

items.pattern: tender meat / steak / lamb · the meat is tender · opposite: tough
items.meaning: soft and easy to cut and chew
items.example: Slow cooking turns a cheap cut into really **tender meat**.
more: The lamb was so **tender** that it fell off the bone.
Marinating chicken in yogurt overnight makes the **meat** really **tender**.
items.watchOut: «Ніжне, м'яке м'ясо» — tender meat. Soft meat звучить дивно (наче розварене), а gentle — лагідний, про людей і рухи.

items.pattern: tough meat / steak · the meat is / goes tough · opposite: tender
items.meaning: hard to cut and chew
items.example: The school dinners were awful: **tough meat** and cold potatoes.
more: Squid goes **tough** and rubbery if you cook it for too long.
This **meat** is so **tough** that the knife just slides off it.
items.watchOut: «Жорстке м'ясо» — зазвичай tough meat, не hard meat і не strict meat. Tough ще означає «важкий» (a tough day) і «міцний, витривалий» (a tough guy).

items.pattern: a sharp knife / pencil / blade · keep knives sharp · opposite: blunt
items.meaning: with a thin edge or point that cuts or draws easily
items.example: You need a really **sharp knife** to slice tomatoes thinly.
more: Bring two **sharp pencils** and a rubber to the exam.
The chef sharpens his **knives** every morning to keep them **sharp**.
items.watchOut: «Гострий» про ніж — sharp. Гостра їжа — hot або spicy, не sharp (sharp про смак — різкий, кислуватий: sharp cheese).

items.pattern: a blunt knife / pencil / blade · go blunt · opposite: sharp
items.meaning: no longer sharp, so it doesn't cut well or draw a thin line
items.example: Cutting onions with a **blunt knife** makes your eyes water even more.
more: My eyebrow **pencil** has gone **blunt**. Have you got a sharpener?
Cooks say a **blunt knife** is more dangerous than a sharp one, because it slips.
items.watchOut: «Тупий» про ніж чи олівець — blunt (американці часто кажуть dull). Не stupid і не dumb: так кажуть про людей. Blunt про людину — прямолінійний, різкий.

items.pattern: ice / snow melts · melt – melted · also butter, chocolate, ice cream melts
items.meaning: turns into water because it gets warmer
items.example: The **snow melted** in a few hours once the sun came out.
more: Drink your lemonade before **the ice melts** and makes it watery.
Put the ice cream back in the freezer before it **melts**.
items.watchOut: «Тане» — melts. Dissolve — розчинятися в рідині (sugar dissolves in tea); про лід і сніг так зазвичай не кажуть.

items.pattern: snow / ice / the ground thaws · frozen food thaws · thaw sth (out)
items.meaning: becomes soft or liquid again after being frozen, because it gets warmer
items.uk: сніг розтає; відтавати (про лід, землю, заморожені продукти)
items.example: In March the **snow** finally **thaws** and the paths turn to mud.
more: Leave the chicken in the fridge overnight so it can **thaw**.
After a week of sunshine, the frozen river began to **thaw**.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /θɔː/, як thought без t. Про сніг можна сказати і melts, і thaws, а про заморожені продукти чи промерзлу землю — thaw (про продукти ще defrost).

items.pattern: fruit goes soft · go – went – gone soft · bananas / tomatoes / pears go soft
items.meaning: becomes too soft because it is getting old
items.example: Eat the peaches today; they're starting to **go soft**.
more: These tomatoes have **gone soft**, so I'll use them in a sauce.
Pears **go soft** very quickly once they're ripe.
items.watchOut: Про зміну на гірше англійці часто кажуть go: go soft, go hard, go bad, go off. Become soft звучить книжно, а make soft — це «зробити м'яким».

items.pattern: bread goes hard · also bread goes stale · cake / cheese goes hard
items.meaning: becomes hard and dry because it is old
items.example: Put the loaf in a bag, or it'll **go hard** by tomorrow.
more: **Bread goes stale** quickly in hot, dry weather.
If you leave the lid off, the icing will **go hard**.
items.watchOut: «Хліб зачерствів» — the bread has gone hard або has gone stale (stale — саме про черствий хліб, печиво, торт). Не the bread has become old.

items.pattern: sb's voice softens (gets friendlier) / hardens (gets less friendly) · soften – softened · harden – hardened
items.meaning: softens: becomes kinder and friendlier; hardens: becomes colder and less friendly
items.example: When she saw how upset her son was, her **voice softened**.
more: The receptionist was polite at first, but her **voice hardened** when I asked for a refund.
Grandpa's **voice softens** whenever he talks about the village where he grew up.
items.watchOut: У soften t не вимовляється: /ˈsɒfn/. Her voice softened — голос став лагіднішим; якщо голос став тихішим — her voice got quieter.

items.pattern: sb's attitude (to / towards sth) softens (gets less severe) / hardens (gets more severe) · attitudes soften / harden
items.meaning: softens: becomes less strict or severe; hardens: becomes stricter and less willing to change
items.example: My parents' **attitude** to tattoos has **softened** over the years.
more: After the third burglary in a month, **attitudes** in the village **hardened**.
The head teacher's **attitude softened** once she heard the whole story.
items.watchOut: Ставлення до когось — attitude to / towards sb, не relation to (relation — зв'язок, родич). Пом'якшилося — softened, стало жорсткішим — hardened.

items.pattern: a matt finish · matt paint / photos / prints · US spelling matte · opposite: gloss
items.meaning: a surface that is not shiny at all
items.example: We chose **matt paint** for the living room because we didn't want shiny walls.
more: The new kitchen tiles have a **matt finish**, so they're not slippery.
**Matt** walls hide small bumps better than shiny ones.
items.watchOut: Матовий — matt (брит.), matte (амер.). Не mat: a mat — килимок. Матове скло — frosted glass, не matt glass.

items.pattern: a gloss finish · gloss paint / photos · also a glossy finish · opposite: matt
items.meaning: a shiny surface that reflects the light
items.example: I'd like these photos printed with a **gloss finish**, please.
more: Our new car has a deep red **gloss finish**.
The new kitchen cupboards have a **high-gloss finish** that shows every fingerprint.
items.watchOut: Глянець — gloss, а не glance (glance — швидкий погляд). Gloss paint, a gloss finish; прикметник glossy — про волосся, журнали (glossy magazines — глянцеві журнали).

items.pattern: a smooth, creamy texture · creamy yogurt / soup / sauce
items.meaning: thick and smooth, like cream
items.example: Blend the soup until it has a smooth, **creamy texture**.
more: Greek yogurt has a thicker, **creamier texture** than ordinary yogurt.
Add a little butter at the end to give the mashed potato a **creamy texture**.
items.watchOut: Консистенція їжі — texture (або consistency), не structure. Creamy — ніжний, як вершки; кремового кольору — cream або cream-coloured.

items.pattern: finely chopped onion / herbs / garlic · chop sth finely · opposite: coarsely / roughly chopped
items.meaning: cut into very small pieces
items.example: Sprinkle some **finely chopped** parsley over the potatoes.
more: The recipe needs one **finely chopped** onion.
Kids eat vegetables more happily when they're **finely chopped**.
items.watchOut: «Дрібно нарізаний» — finely chopped, не small chopped: перед chopped потрібен прислівник. Тонко нарізаний скибочками — thinly sliced.

items.pattern: coarsely / roughly chopped · chop sth coarsely / roughly · opposite: finely chopped
items.meaning: cut into large, uneven pieces
items.example: Add two **coarsely chopped** carrots to the stew.
more: **Roughly chop** the potatoes and boil them with the skins on.
I like my onions **coarsely chopped**, so you can see them in the soup.
items.watchOut: «Крупно нарізати» — chop coarsely або roughly, не largely: largely означає «здебільшого». Coarsely вимовляється /ˈkɔːsli/.

items.pattern: coarse(-grain) salt · coarse sand · coarse grains · opposite: fine salt / sand / grains
items.meaning: made of large grains, not small ones
items.example: I always keep a jar of **coarse sea salt** next to the cooker.
more: Rub **coarse salt** into the pork skin to make good crackling.
**Coarse** grains of salt take longer to dissolve than fine ones.
items.watchOut: Крупна сіль — coarse salt, не big salt і не large salt (хоча large grains — великі зерна — можна). Coarse /kɔːs/ звучить так само, як course.

items.pattern: crushed garlic / ice / biscuits · crush garlic
items.meaning: pressed hard until it breaks into small pieces or a paste
items.example: Fry the onion, then add two cloves of **crushed garlic**.
more: **Crushed** biscuits make a great base for a cheesecake.
The sauce needs a clove of **crushed garlic** and a squeeze of lemon.
items.watchOut: Розчавлений часник — зазвичай crushed garlic (американці ще кажуть minced). Squeeze — видавлювати сік (squeeze a lemon); про часник так не кажуть.

items.pattern: glossy hair / fur / coat · glossy magazines · opposite: dull hair
items.meaning: shiny and smooth in a healthy, attractive way
items.example: Since she started eating more fish, she's had beautiful **glossy hair**.
more: Our cat has a lovely **glossy** black **coat**.
The salon promised me **glossy hair**, but it just looked greasy.
items.watchOut: Блискуче, здорове волосся — glossy або shiny hair, не brilliant hair і не glittering hair. Тьмяне волосся — dull hair.

items.pattern: greasy hands / fingers · greasy marks · also oily hands
items.meaning: covered in oil or fat
items.example: I always end up with **greasy hands** after eating fried chicken.
more: The cupboards near the cooker always get **greasy**.
Never touch a camera lens with **greasy fingers**.
items.watchOut: Масні руки — greasy (або oily) hands. Fat hands — це «товсті руки», а fatty — жирний про їжу: fatty meat.

items.pattern: sticky fingers / hands · sticky with jam / honey · a sticky table / floor
items.meaning: covered with something like jam or honey that makes things stick to them
items.example: Toffee apples are fun to eat, but you end up with **sticky fingers**.
more: Pass me a wet wipe; my **fingers** are **sticky** from the orange.
The cinema floor was **sticky** with spilt cola.
items.watchOut: Липкий — sticky, не sticking (sticking — той, що застряг чи прилипає саме зараз). Жартома have sticky fingers — бути нечистим на руку.

items.pattern: sth goes smoothly · go – went – gone smoothly · also run smoothly
items.meaning: happen without any problems; go well
items.example: Our move to the new flat **went smoothly**: nothing got broken.
more: I hope everything **goes smoothly** at your interview tomorrow.
The wedding **went smoothly** until the best man lost the rings.
items.watchOut: «Пройшло гладко» — went smoothly, з -ly. Passed smoothly зазвичай не кажуть: pass — це «минати» (про час).

items.pattern: have (got) a sharp tongue · a sharp-tongued person
items.meaning: often say unkind, critical things to people
items.example: My aunt **has a sharp tongue**, so nobody argues with her at family dinners.
more: Be careful what you tell the manager; she's got **a sharp tongue**.
He's kind really, despite his **sharp tongue**.
items.watchOut: A sharp tongue — «злий, колючий язик»: людина каже неприємні речі. Якщо «гострий на язик» означає «дотепний» — witty. Не acute tongue і не spicy tongue.

items.pattern: be in / get into / get out of a sticky situation · informal
items.meaning: a difficult or awkward situation that is hard to get out of
items.example: We got into **a sticky situation** when our car broke down far from any village.
more: Lying to your parents will only get you into **a sticky situation** later.
My brother is great at getting out of **sticky situations**.
items.watchOut: Халепа, скрутне становище — a sticky situation (розмовне) або a tricky / difficult situation. «Гостра ситуація» — зазвичай не sharp situation, а a tense або critical situation.

items.pattern: coarse jokes / humour / language · also crude / dirty jokes
items.meaning: rude, vulgar jokes in bad taste
items.example: My grandad laughs at **coarse jokes** that make my mum blush.
more: I don't find **coarse jokes** funny; they're just rude.
His **coarse language** shocked the other parents at the football match.
items.watchOut: «Грубі, непристойні жарти» — coarse jokes (також crude, rude або dirty jokes), не rough jokes. Coarse /kɔːs/ звучить так само, як course, але пишеться інакше.

items.pattern: a velvety sky · also a velvety voice / skin / texture
items.meaning: a dark, deep sky that looks soft and smooth, like velvet cloth
items.example: From the mountain hut we watched the stars come out in the **velvety sky**.
more: The cat's ears are soft and **velvety**.
Peaches have a soft, **velvety skin**.
items.watchOut: Оксамит — velvet, «як оксамит» — velvety /ˈvelvəti/. Velvet перед іменником зазвичай означає «з оксамиту» (a velvet dress).

warmup.uk: Якщо я не мию голову щодня, волосся стає жирним.
warmup.q: If I don't wash it every day, my hair gets ___.
warmup.explain: Жирне волосся — greasy (або oily) hair. Fat — товстий, fatty — жирний про їжу.

warmup.uk: Цей ніж зовсім тупий, ним нічого не розріжеш.
warmup.q: This knife is completely ___; it won't cut anything.
warmup.explain: Тупий ніж — a blunt knife. Stupid і dumb — про людей.
Ніжне м'ясо — tender. Gentle — лагідний (про людей, рухи), mild — м'який на смак чи про погоду.

warmup.uk: Через грозу політ був дуже тряский.
warmup.q: The flight was really ___ because of the storm.
warmup.explain: Тряский політ чи дорога — bumpy. Shaking і trembling — «труситься», «тремтить», так політ не описують.

warmup.q: The bread in the kitchen has already gone ___.
warmup.explain: Хліб зачерствів — has gone hard або has gone stale. Gone old так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Мама додає в суп дрібно нарізану моркву.
warmup.q: Mum adds ___ chopped carrots to the soup.
warmup.explain: Дрібно нарізаний — finely chopped. Перед chopped потрібен прислівник, тому не small і не little.

warmup.uk: Для цього рецепта потрібна крупна морська сіль.
warmup.explain: Крупна сіль — coarse salt. Вимова /kɔːs/, як course.

warmup.uk: Наш тренер має гострий язик, тому всі його бояться.
warmup.q: Our coach has a ___ tongue, so everyone's afraid of him.
warmup.explain: Гострий (злий) язик — a sharp tongue. Spicy — гострий про їжу, acute — гострий про біль чи кут.

A.q: I'm not coming on the boat trip: I get seasick when the water is ___.
A.explain: Неспокійна вода з дрібними хвилями — choppy (або rough). Nervous — про людей, tough — жорсткий, міцний.

A.q: Our taxi went down a ___ country lane full of holes, and my head hit the roof twice.
A.explain: Вибоїста, тряска дорога — a bumpy road / lane. Shaky — хиткий, тремтячий; choppy — про воду з дрібними хвилями.

A.q: Sorry about the steak. It's a bit ___: I left it on the grill too long.
A.explain: Жорстке м'ясо — tough meat. Strict — суворий (про людей, правила), rigid — негнучкий.

B.q: The ice on the pond will ___ once the temperature goes above zero.
B.explain: Лід і сніг розтають — thaw (або melt). Dissolve — розчинятися в рідині, evaporate — випаровуватися.

B.q: These bananas are over a week old, and they've gone ___.
B.explain: Фрукти м'якнуть від старості — go soft. Tender — про м'ясо, weak — слабкий.

B.q: At first the landlord said no, but his attitude ___ when we offered to pay for the repairs ourselves.
B.explain: Ставлення пом'якшилося — attitude softened. Weakened — ослабло, loosened — послабилося (про вузол, ремінь).

C.q: Matt paint isn't shiny, but ___ paint is.
C.explain: Глянцева фарба — gloss paint (або glossy). Glance — швидкий погляд, glare — сліпуче світло.

C.q: For garlic bread, mix soft butter with some ___ garlic and parsley.
C.explain: Розчавлений часник — crushed garlic. Squeeze — видавлювати сік (squeeze a lemon).

C.q: There's jam on your chin, and your fingers are all ___.
C.explain: Липкі пальці — sticky fingers. Greasy — масні, від жиру, а не від варення.

D.q: The operation ___ smoothly, and she was home the next day.
Losing your passport on holiday can put you in a ___ situation.
D.explain: Скрутне, незручне становище — a sticky situation (розмовне). «Гостра ситуація» — не sharp situation.

D.q: His ___ jokes offended half the guests.
D.explain: Грубі, вульгарні жарти — coarse jokes. Course /kɔːs/ звучить так само, але це «курс».

Chlorine from the pool left her with ___ hair that felt like straw.
Don't use that heavy conditioner near your roots, or you'll end up with ___ hair by lunchtime.
My teenage son washes his hair every morning because it gets ___ so quickly.
This shampoo for ___ hair removes extra oil without drying out your scalp.
Her ___ skin looks shiny in photos, so she always uses powder.
Choose a light, oil-free moisturiser if you have ___ skin.
Sand the old door until the wood has a completely ___ surface.
Her face cream promises ___ skin with no lines or spots.
Years of sunbathing gave her a rough complexion, but her sister, who always wore a hat, still has a ___ complexion.
The cat's tongue feels ___, like sandpaper.
The walls had a ___ surface, so we had to fill and sand them before painting.
Sailors' faces are often ___ and red from the wind and salt.
There wasn't a breath of wind, and the sea was as ___ as glass.
The children can swim today because the sea is nice and ___.
The wind picked up in the afternoon and the water became ___, so the little ferry rocked from side to side.
All ferries are cancelled today because of ___ seas.
The ___ water made it hard to row the little boat back to the beach.
The pilot said we could expect a ___ flight with no turbulence.
They've just resurfaced the road, so it's lovely and ___ now.

example.title: A weekend at the coast
example.uk:
Наші вихідні на узбережжі почалися невдало. Пором запізнився через бурхливе море, а дорога до кемпінгу була така вибоїста, що половина яєць розбилася.

Тієї ночі ми спали на твердій землі, тож уранці всі були не в гуморі. Але потім усе пішло гладко. Море було спокійне, визирнуло сонце, а тато приготував рагу з дуже ніжним м'ясом.

Діти повернулися з пляжу з липкими пальцями, бо їхнє морозиво розтануло на спеці. Увечері ми сиділи надворі під оксамитовим небом, усипаним зорями. Навіть бабуся, в якої гострий язик, сказала, що це були найкращі вихідні за все літо.
example.en:
Our weekend at the coast didn't start well. The ferry was late because of [[rough seas|a7]], and the road to the campsite was so [[bumpy|a9]] that half the eggs broke.

That night we slept on the [[hard ground|a11]], so by morning everyone was grumpy. But after that, things began to [[go smoothly|d1]]. The [[sea was calm|a6]], the sun came out, and Dad cooked a stew with beautifully [[tender meat|a12]].

The children came back from the beach with [[sticky fingers|c10]] because their ice creams had [[melted|b1]] in the heat. In the evening we sat outside under a [[velvety sky|d5]] full of stars. Even Grandma, who [[has a sharp tongue|d2]], said it was the best weekend of the summer.
